title: Model registry CreateModelVersion prompt branch: select prompt handling only when the effective is_prompt tag is 'true'
answers: Why was a model version tagged mlflow.prompt.is_prompt=false treated as a prompt and skipped source validation?
How are duplicate tag keys resolved when creating a model version through the REST API?
What decides whether _create_model_version uses the prompt branch or regular source validation?
Why does a model version with a duplicate is_prompt tag not show up as a prompt?
body:
Path: CreateModelVersion requests that carry tags enter mlflow/server/handlers.py:_create_model_version, where mlflow/server/handlers.py:_is_prompt_request decides between the prompt branch (_validate_prompt_source) and the regular branch (_validate_source_run / _validate_source_model).
Rule: _is_prompt_request collapses request_message.tags into a dict keyed by tag key, so the last value wins, and returns true only when the effective IS_PROMPT_TAG_KEY value lowercased equals 'true'. This mirrors ModelVersion._is_prompt. Checking only for the presence of a key is wrong, because the stored entity then differs from what the handler routed.
Symptom: A model version created with mlflow.prompt.is_prompt set to 'false' took the prompt path, so source-run and source-model validation were skipped. With duplicate tags [true, false], the handler took the prompt path while the persisted entity was not a prompt.
Constraints: Only the effective final value matters, so [true, false] is not a prompt and [false, true] is. Any non-'true' value, including '0' or empty, uses regular source validation and returns 'Invalid model version source' for traversal sources.
applies: Prompt-versus-regular dispatch for CreateModelVersion requests in mlflow/server/handlers.py; not the client-side ModelVersion property.
says: Setting the prompt tag to false still treated the model version as a prompt.
Model versions with false prompt tags should not skip standard model source checks.
Duplicate tags on a new model version should resolve using the last value provided.
Registering a regular model with a negative prompt flag triggered the wrong validation.
search: Dispatching CreateModelVersion requests in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_create_model_version selects prompt handling only when mlflow/server/handlers.py:_is_prompt_request evaluates the effective IS_PROMPT_TAG_KEY value lowercased to 'true'. Tag entries in request_message.tags are collapsed into a dictionary where the last value wins, mirroring ModelVersion._is_prompt rather than checking key presence. Previously, setting mlflow.prompt.is_prompt to 'false' or having duplicate tags like [true, false] routed requests to the prompt path, bypassing _validate_source_run and _validate_source_model. Any non-'true' value such as '0' or empty falls back to regular source validation, and the rule does not apply to client-side ModelVersion properties.
